comments.body:
## Update: the eleventh run landed, and it is the new worst case

`rb-spree-tax-provider-interface` (adjudicated 2026-09-15, Fleiss κ 0.851, zero contested)
emitted **25 findings that reduce to 15 distinct issues — +67%**, exceeding the `ts-carbon`
+50% cited above. `same_arm_merges` = 11, across **8 duplicate groups**, three of them
three-member.

Revised totals across all **11** four-arm runs: **164 emitted → 137 distinct, +19.7%** (was
+13.9% over 10 runs).

### The spree groups

| issue | rebar members (id / criteria / band) |
|---|---|
| 1.1 | `fe9362212ee777e1b` [E1,COH] blocking · `fe4973736fd1cec19` [E3] advisory |
| 2.1 | `f4bd59683171f9ef2` [E4] blocking · `fee2ecdefb4a472fd` [G1G2] blocking |
| 4.1 | `f808aa9b1ff1a1a44` [G1G2] blocking · `f9787d46f01fa1024` [G6] blocking |
| 6.1 | `fd2ab9187e0f1af59` [E1,E6] · `f867ddb18c92babcc` [T2] · `f733d5b9d1c96f596` [E5] |
| 11.1 | `fb6f563673ec04b82` [A1] · `f5bfe8629b7309691` [E4] |
| 12.1 | `fa97557f732cede1d` [T4] · `f9a1fafd8662260f0` [T11] · `f1cb101798e624148` [T11] |
| 16.1 | `fdac6206d2c64d0d5` [T5a] · `fb617713d8f0ac36b` [T5b] |
| 23.1 | `fbcd188a4af1f9c5c` [G6] · `f88e7e6caacfdf7a1` [E4] |

Group 12.1 is notable: **two of its three members carry the SAME criterion, `T11`** — so the
pattern is not only cross-criterion. The `G1G2`/`G6` shape still recurs (groups 2.1, 4.1, 23.1).

### Correction to "fingerprints do not match": one genuine id collision exists, and it is not a duplicate

Ballot items `2.1` and `2.2` both carry finding id `f4bd59683171f9ef2`. That is **one** finding
the ballot builder split into two parts, not two findings colliding — so it does not contradict
the finding above. Stated explicitly because a reader scanning ids would otherwise read it as a
counterexample. Every genuine duplicate pair in all 11 runs still has **distinct** ids.

### Drop reasons: two more, still no deduplication

The `rfi` verdict's 7 drops were all `veto:cited-reference-inaccurate`. The `spree` verdict also
has 7 drops, under **two different reasons — `low-validity` and `veto:absence-refuted`**. So
across the two sampled verdicts there are three distinct drop reasons and **none of them is
deduplication**. The drop mechanism exists and fires; it just never fires for this.

### Blocking

6 of the 19 member findings in spree's duplicate groups carry `decision=block`, including two
groups (2.1 and 4.1) blocking on **every** member. Consistent with the pattern already recorded.

### Divergent blocking eligibility within one issue — more instances

Group 1.1: `blocking_enabled=true, threshold=0.6` against `blocking_enabled=false,
threshold=0.95`. Group 11.1 and 23.1 show the same split. One issue, two different answers to
"can this block?".

Closing as a DUPLICATE of longish-ripe-snowyowl (2331-3e0e-f880-4837), which was filed first for the same defect and is referenced from the study's results document. All evidence from this ticket — the 11-run totals, the 24 duplicate groups, the fingerprint finding, the three drop reasons, the blocking counts and the divergent blocking eligibility — has been consolidated onto that ticket as a comment. Linked `duplicates`.

Why this happened, recorded because it is a search hazard others will hit: I searched the tracker before filing and concluded no such bug existed. The existing ticket's title does contain "duplicates", so a title filter should have matched it — but it was not in the result set my full-text search returned at all. I filtered a capped/ranked result list and treated it as the whole corpus. A negative result from `rebar search` is not proof of absence.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

In a controlled plan-review study, rebar emitted **multiple separate findings that independent
classifiers judged to be one and the same issue**. Across 10 plan reviews (one rebar run each,
`bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`, runner `pydantic_ai`), rebar emitted **139 findings that
reduce to 122 distinct issues — +13.9% inflation**. It is not evenly spread:

| run (study id) | emitted | distinct | inflation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ts-carbon-dsx-card-web-component` | 15 | 10 | **+50%** |
| `ts-strata-paidleave-rfi-staff-experience` | 15 | 11 | **+36%** |
| `ruby-mn-deed-casemgmt-outbound-writeback` | 9 | 7 | **+29%** |
| `jira-dso-legacy-code-remediation` | 18 | 15 | **+20%** |
| `java-opensearch-adaptive-concurrency` | 19 | 18 | +6% |
| `jira-dso-strata-sdk-planning-context` | 19 | 18 | +6% |
| `scss-uswds-elements-dsx-token-migration` | 20 | 19 | +5% |
| `java-gradle`, `java-iceberg`, `ts-strata-sdk-cm-signal-coverage` | — | — | 0% |

"Same issue" is not my judgment: each run was classified by **three independent judges** who
answered a generated list of relation candidates, and a pair was merged only on a **2-of-3
majority**. 16 duplicate groups resulted.

## Which findings duplicated, and from which criteria

The recurring shape is **a specific criterion and a generic one reporting the same defect**. In
**13 of 16** groups at least one member came from `G1G2` (edit-set/scope accuracy) or `G6`
(approach soundness). Full inventory (`id` is the per-finding id in the verdict JSON):

**`ts-strata-paidleave-rfi-staff-experience`** (4 groups)
- fulfill-endpoint idempotency: `f02d0cd5760121153` [T5b,T9] + `f50f3f76a15e65bc6` [G6]
- outbound auth/prior-art: `fd2b4ab546f9e330c` [T1] + `f252cc4922c662cc3` [T5c]
- 3-way: `ff1e44af24964e2c6` [E4] + `f711f89314e759479` [G1G2] + `ff433167f9a0c74c5` [G6]
- send-flow failure handling: `f71d6f4d69d9eda6e` [T5b] + `fa13c03bbc6396a28` [T6]

**`ts-carbon-dsx-card-web-component`** (3 groups)
- `fafd331051f282d48` [A1] + `fce6a492c25ad79d8` [G1G2]
- 4-way: `fac2282ff04867c07` [E4] + `f73a2ac0bd5912fa0` [G1G2] + `fae54d7542a904816` [T1] + `f7cb2731aec88a265` [T3]
- `f036b5d8ba8ce1922` [E4] + `f5677bcc33d08f796` [G1G2]

**`jira-dso-legacy-code-remediation`** (2 groups, both 3-way)
- `fefb33dc413d1ffce` [E2,T2] + `ff3ca4c59c47d2605` [T5a] + `f979dd7afcdc2675a` [G6]
- `f183d47c0909708aa` [E2] + `fa60c9c99e3cf1eb4` [T5b] + `f979dd7afcdc2675a` [G6]

**`scss-uswds-elements-dsx-token-migration`**: `fa397c3a9c775bb37` [E2] + `f2fe1f5b397e2040f` [G1G2]; `f8fbdb6fdf4b8abc3` [COH,E6] + `f164935f57c7fe71a` [G6]
**`java-opensearch-adaptive-concurrency`**: `f5b48e0266cef5b37` [E2,E1] + `f45ee8af458d5e534` [A1]; `fec86f00ba47d9527` [G1G2] + `f6df8eee7ef8c8679` [T3]
**`ruby-mn-deed-casemgmt-outbound-writeback`**: `fbda6e01e068e5510` [COH] + `f4439faeb93f9d19d` [E1]; `f8c8cc7182e9ee590` [E4] + `f72dae17551bf761a` [G1G2]
**`jira-dso-strata-sdk-planning-context`**: `f596c92c78cf6b105` [G6] + `faf7819abb3a020d4` [T8]

Worth noting for whoever picks this up: `f979dd7afcdc2675a` [G6] is **one** finding that was
merged into **two different** issues in the same run — it duplicates two distinct defects at once.

## Fingerprints: they do NOT match

**All 16 groups have fully distinct per-finding `id`s — 16/16 all-distinct, zero collisions.**
So whatever identity these ids carry, duplicate findings are not colliding on it and could not
be caught by equality on it.

There is no per-finding fingerprint field to compare. `material_fingerprint` exists only **once
per run** at the top level of the verdict (e.g. `ca0fee4a8c160bf4`), not per finding.

## Were duplicates dropped? No.

The verdict `dropped` list is populated — 7 entries on the `rfi` run — but **every drop is
`reason: veto:cited-reference-inaccurate`**, a citation-accuracy veto. **No finding in any run
was dropped for duplication.** Every duplicate reached the emitted output.

## Were they blocking? Yes — 22 of the ~35 member findings.

This is not confined to advisory noise. Whole groups are blocking on **every** copy:
`scss-uswds` 1.1 and 3.1, `ts-carbon` 2.1 and 3.1, `rfi` 3.1 and 6.1, `mn-deed` 2.1,
`dso-strata` 1.1, `java-opensearch` 5.1. Duplication therefore inflates the **blocking** count a
plan author must answer, not just the advisory tail.

## Other observations an investigator may want

1. **Blocking eligibility diverges between copies of one issue.** `rfi` group 12.1:
   `f02d0cd5760121153` has `blocking_enabled=false, block_threshold=0.95` while its duplicate
   `f50f3f76a15e65bc6` has `blocking_enabled=true, block_threshold=0.6`. Same issue, different
   eligibility and a threshold 0.35 apart. Also in `java-opensearch` 3.2, `dso-legacy` 10.1 and
   14.1, `ts-carbon` 9.1, `mn-deed` 1.1.
2. **Copies often carry identical confidence.** `rfi` 12.1: both `validity=0.75`, both
   `priority=0.5025`. `ts-carbon` 2.1: all four at `validity=0.8`. `dso-legacy` 10.1: all three
   at `0.875`. Not universal — `scss-uswds` 1.1 is 1.0 vs 0.9.
3. **`cohort` is sometimes much wider than `criteria`.** `f02d0cd5760121153` has
   `criteria=['T5b','T9']` but `cohort=['T2','T4','T5b','T5e','T7','T9']`.
4. **Every criterion involved in a duplicate group is `blocking` or `advisory` per
   `rebar explain`**; `G1G2`, `G6`, `E4`, `T1`, `T3`, `A1` are all `exec:AGENT`, while `E1`,
   `E2`, `COH`, `T5b`, `T9` are `1-TURN`/`2-STEP`. Recorded as observation only.
5. **Two runs show 0% inflation** (`java-gradle`, `java-iceberg`, plus `signal-coverage`), so
   this is not unconditional.

## Reproduction material

Verdict JSONs: `~/plan-review-bakeoff/wave3/rebar-runs/<run-id>.verdict.json`.
Judge-majority merges: `~/plan-review-bakeoff/artifacts/adjudications/<run-id>.adjudication.json`,
field `merged_issues` (members + arms), and `arms.rebar.same_arm_merges`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Root cause identified for why one defect is emitted as several findings under different criteria.
- [ ] Stated explicitly whether any de-duplication step is expected to run before emission, and if so why it did not fire on these 16 groups.
- [ ] Decision recorded on whether per-finding identity should support duplicate detection, given the observed ids are all distinct and `material_fingerprint` is per-run.
- [ ] The divergent `blocking_enabled`/`block_threshold` between copies of one issue is explained or fixed.
- [ ] Regression coverage over at least the `ts-carbon` (+50%) and `rfi` (+36%) cases.

## Out of scope

Root-causing was deliberately **not** attempted here; this ticket is an evidence record.
compiled_state.title: Plan review emits one defect as several findings under different criteria (+14% finding inflation, up to +50%; duplicates not deduped and often blocking)
